headline: Inflation breaks 6 percent, yet markets log a third weekly gain

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Saturday, the fourteenth of November, and this is your Market Brief.

Three things matter most this morning. First, inflation has crossed the Reserve Bank's comfort ceiling. Retail inflation rose to 6.09 percent in October, the ninth straight monthly rise, and economists now openly talk about another rate hike in December.

Second, the trade gap has blown out. India's goods trade deficit hit a one-year high of 39.88 billion dollars in October, as costlier energy pushed imports to a record.

And third, despite all that, and despite the turmoil around Nvidia overseas, Indian shares ended a third straight week of gains. Let's take it from there.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Friday's session was a cautious one. The bank, auto and realty indices each slipped about 1 percent as the inflation number stoked fears of a rate hike. Even so, Business Standard reports that Indian markets extended their gains for a third straight week, holding up while artificial intelligence stocks around the world came under pressure.

The standout this week was public sector banks. The Nifty PSU Bank index rose 8 percent over the week, its best weekly run in seven months, taking it to its highest level since March. Punjab National Bank led the pack, up 13.3 percent to 143 rupees.

Power stocks were in demand on Friday after reports that the national transmission committee approved a first-of-its-kind 1,150 kilovolt line worth 68,816 crore rupees. Oil-sensitive names went the other way. Bharat Petroleum and IndiGo fell over 2 percent as crude hovered near 95 dollars.

Among single stocks, Paytm crossed its November 2021 listing price of 1,950 rupees for the first time in nearly five years. The Reserve Bank had given in-principle approval for its wallet business. And Reliance has rebounded 15 percent this month after its results.

On flows, Livemint notes that foreign institutional investors and stronger earnings have powered the rally, while domestic institutions have kept selling.

The rupee weakened to 94.25 to the dollar, and the ten-year government bond yield rose six basis points to 7.31 percent.

Now the levels to watch. Moneycontrol's technical view says a break below 25,000 on the Nifty could extend profit booking, with key support at 24,800 to 24,700. On the upside, a move above the recent swing high of 25,425 could trigger a sharp rally. And one date for your calendar: MSCI's index changes take effect on the thirtieth of November. Coforge and LIC are expected to draw inflows, while PI Industries may see outflows.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
Now to the primary market, which is about to get busy.

The big one: Mahanadi Coalfields is likely to open its first public offer next week. Coal India plans to sell up to 66.18 crore shares, a 10 percent stake, in an offer for sale estimated at around 9,500 crore rupees, or roughly a billion dollars.

Crystal Crop Protection opens for subscription on the eighteenth, with a grey market premium of nearly 17 percent. And Watrana Rentals launches a 120 crore rupee issue on the nineteenth, made up entirely of fresh shares, priced between 232 and 245 rupees.

Further out, SEBI has cleared three big names: Razorpay, MakeMyTrip India and Sembcorp Green Infra. Razorpay reportedly plans to raise about 600 million dollars. And Haldiram Snacks Food has reportedly appointed EY to prepare for a listing that could raise about 10,000 crore rupees.

On the deals side, SoftBank sold a 1.65 percent stake in Meesho for 1,885 crore rupees. Sixteen buyers stepped in, with Fidelity the largest at about 573 crore rupees.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
Now to results, starting with capital goods and defence. Hitachi Energy shares jumped 12 percent after its September quarter orders rose 86 percent to about 4,121 crore rupees. Profit rose 21 percent, and its order backlog hit a record 33,335 crore rupees. Among the defence companies, HAL and GRSE grew profits by 16 and 12 percent. But Bharat Dynamics saw profit fall 15 percent on margin pressure, and its shares slipped 3 percent.

In pharma, Alkem Labs' net profit fell 14 percent to 667 crore rupees, and the stock lost 3 percent.

Over in financials, Manappuram Finance fell 4 percent after its results, even though CLSA upgraded it to outperform with a target of 370 rupees. Turtlemint's quarterly loss narrowed about 67 percent to 25.83 crore rupees, and the stock hit its 5 percent upper circuit.

In technology, Black Box posted a 30 percent rise in profit to 73 crore rupees, with revenue up 22 percent to 1,936 crore and a record order book of 1.04 billion dollars.

On the weaker side, Ola Electric's revenue fell 39 percent. Its loss narrowed to 362 crore rupees, but the shares fell nearly 7 percent. Vodafone Idea's loss was wider than expected, and Park Medi World tumbled 10 percent as profit fell 31 percent.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
Now to the economy, where inflation is the story.

Retail inflation rose to 6.09 percent in October, up from 5.54 percent in September, breaching the Reserve Bank's upper tolerance limit of 6 percent. Food inflation is close to 9 percent, onion prices are up 116 percent, and six states have crossed 7 percent. It's spreading, too. Inflation in mobile phones climbed to 8.65 percent, with laptops close behind.

So what will the Reserve Bank do? ICICI Bank expects a 25 basis point hike in December. Nuvama says uneven monsoons and a possible El Nino keep another hike on the table. Axis Mutual Fund goes further, and expects another 50 to 75 basis points of hikes.

But there's a counterpoint. Chief Economic Adviser V Anantha Nageswaran warned that supply shocks are making rate hikes less effective, and said fiscal policy will have to do more of the work.

On trade, the October goods deficit widened to 39.88 billion dollars, a one-year high, and well above the 32.25 billion that a Reuters poll expected. Exports hit a record, but energy prices pushed imports to a record 89.35 billion. One bright spot: gold imports fell about 63 percent in October, to 5.51 billion dollars, as global prices dropped.

On growth, SBI Research expects September quarter growth of 7.8 percent, ahead of the Reserve Bank's estimate of 7.2 percent.

From the Cabinet, the rabi fertiliser subsidy has been set at 62,370 crore rupees, up 64 percent, with the price of DAP held at 1,350 rupees a bag. The Cabinet also cleared a 5,000 crore rupee credit guarantee fund for MUDRA loans. And the government has notified commodity contracts as financial products at GIFT City, opening the door for global trading firms.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Around the world, it was a rough day for technology. Wall Street ended lower as the turmoil around Nvidia weighed on chip stocks. AMD fell almost 10 percent and Nvidia lost over 4 percent, while stubborn inflation keeps bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike alive.

Microsoft had a bad day too. A global outage of more than 12 hours hit Outlook, Teams and Copilot in more than 70 countries. Its shares fell about 2.5 percent.

Oil is set for a second weekly decline on growing signs of a supply surplus, even as President Trump sticks with the blockade on Iran. Brent was around 95 dollars a barrel.

And gold is heading for its worst week since June, after touching its lowest level in more than a year as rate hike bets build. Mirae Asset Sharekhan thinks it could slip further, to test 3,750 dollars an ounce.

segments.title: Stories you're following
segments.script: An update on the India–US trade deal you're following. The United States has assured India of lower tariffs than its trading rivals under the proposed deal. The first phase will cover goods only, with services left for a later phase. But the final tariff framework hinges on an American Section 301 probe into forced labour, and both sides are said to be aiming to finish by the G20 Summit in Florida.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Finally, your money.

With rate hikes in the air, fixed deposit rates are rising. Bank of Baroda raised its 555-day deposit rate by 10 basis points, to 6.90 percent for regular customers and 7.50 percent for super senior citizens.

HDFC Mutual Fund has launched its first specialised investment fund, a hybrid long-short strategy that can take short positions of up to 25 percent of assets. The new fund offer runs until the twenty-seventh, with a minimum investment of 10 lakh rupees.

One for your clients who run payrolls: employers must file the October return and deposit provident fund contributions by tomorrow, the fifteenth, to avoid interest and penalties.

On the professional front, the Bombay Chartered Accountants' Society has urged SEBI to let CA firms monitor the use of funds in smaller issues, and to make monitoring agencies flag related-party payments. And YES Bank has asked the Supreme Court to review its October ruling against the write-down of 8,415 crore rupees of additional tier one bonds.

A reminder from the tax side: buying property in a spouse's or parent's name with your own money can draw income tax scrutiny and action under the benami law.

That's your brief. Here's what to watch. The provident fund deadline is tomorrow. Next week brings the Mahanadi Coalfields offer, Crystal Crop on the eighteenth and Watrana on the nineteenth, along with wholesale inflation data and the minutes of the Federal Reserve's last meeting. On the Nifty, 25,000 is the line traders are watching. Have a good weekend.
